title: Thirty-one years, 22 moments
lede: From a magazine ad for a watch to a licence worth $100M. Filter by thread.

events.title: Founded
events.text: The company is founded; Thalheimer’s first hit is a waterproof runner’s watch sold through a magazine ad.

events.title: The first catalog
events.text: The first Sharper Image catalog is mailed.

events.title: Into stores
events.text: The company begins opening its own stores.

events.title: Public
events.text: Sharper Image goes public.

events.title: Online
events.text: The company starts selling online.

events.title: First review
events.text: Consumer Reports reviews the Ionic Breeze.

events.title: 127 stores
events.text: Fiscal 2002: $513.8M of revenue, comparable-store sales up 13.6%.

events.title: Second review
events.text: Consumer Reports criticises the Ionic Breeze Quadra again; Sharper Image sues Consumers Union.

events.title: Best profit
events.text: Fiscal 2003 net earnings reach $21.0M on $647.5M of revenue.

events.title: The peak
events.text: Fiscal 2004 revenue is $760.0M; air purifiers are 40.0% of it. 175 stores.

events.title: Suit thrown out
events.text: A federal judge grants Consumers Union’s anti-SLAPP motion and strikes the complaint.
Sharper Image drops its appeal and pays Consumers Union’s fees and costs.

events.title: First loss
events.text: Fiscal 2005 revenue falls to $669.0M; net loss of $16.1M; comparable-store sales down 16.0%.

events.title: Proxy settlement
events.text: Knightspoint, owner of 12.8% of the shares, wins board seats without a vote.

events.title: Founder out
events.text: Richard Thalheimer departs as chairman and CEO; Jerry W. Levin becomes interim CEO.
Fiscal 2006 revenue is $525.3M and the net loss $59.9M. Air purifiers fall to 23.4% of revenue.

events.title: Another 26% gone
events.text: Sales for the year to January 31, 2008 fall to $374.9M.

events.title: Chapter 11
events.text: The company files in Delaware with 184 stores.

events.title: Suspended
events.text: Nasdaq suspends the shares; delisting follows in April.

events.title: Sold for $49M
events.text: Gordon Brothers and Hilco buy the name, the catalog, the website and the inventory. Store closing sales began May 31.

events.title: TSIC, Inc.
events.text: The company gives up its name, as the sale agreement required.

events.title: Iconix buys the brand
events.text: Iconix Brand Group pays $65.65M for the trademark and related rights.

events.title: $100M
events.text: Iconix sells the brand to ThreeSixty Group, its largest licensee.

events.title: Still selling
events.text: sharperimage.com trades as an online gadget shop.
